prompt: Use case: illustration-story. Asset: wide 16:9 hero for a portfolio case study about The Design Dash, an open design process. Create a beautiful editorial illustration showing a fictional neighborhood tool library as the running example. Warm ivory background, graphite ink, mustard yellow accents matching an existing yellow portfolio, restrained muted sage. Clean hand-crafted architectural illustration, subtle paper texture, precise typography, generous negative space. Composition: left a small sketch of a neighborhood tool shelf with a cordless drill, sander, toolbox; center a person borrowing a drill with a librarian; right a large elegant simplified app wireframe displaying a drill and a borrowing record. Under the composition three clear compact labels, exactly "Find a tool", "Borrow it", "Return it". Small unobtrusive text at upper left exactly "EXAMPLE DASH · NEIGHBORHOOD TOOL LIBRARY". Not a generic flowchart, not boxes joined by arrows. Visually engaging and easy to understand. No brands, no cannabis, no made-up research statistics, no sales pitch. Show complete uncropped objects, no tiny illegible paragraphs. This is an illustrative made-up example, not evidence from a real project.

Use case: infographic-diagram. Asset: landscape 3:2 editorial teaching image for The Design Dash. Fictional example neighborhood tool library. Show how OOUX becomes three Object Guides in an Object Library. Warm ivory, graphite, mustard yellow highlights, muted sage, crisp large typography with subtle paper material. Beautiful organized tabletop with three LARGE document cards, clearly distinct and equally legible; small realistic illustrated cordless drill on TOOL card, membership card on MEMBER card, return slip on LOAN card. Headline exactly "Name the objects before the screens". Cards exact text: first "TOOL", "Cordless drill", "Attributes", "Name · Condition", "Actions", "View · Request"; second "MEMBER", "Library member", "Attributes", "Name · Member ID", "Actions", "Browse · Request"; third "LOAN", "Borrowing record", "Attributes", "Tool · Member · Due date", "Actions", "Check out · Return". Along bottom a single simple relation reads "A Member borrows a Tool through a Loan." Under LOAN card show compact lifecycle strip "Requested → Checked out → Returned". Small corner label "ILLUSTRATIVE OBJECT GUIDES". These are guide excerpts, not a software UI. Avoid numerous connectors, 3D extrusions, ornamental gradients, extra text, logos. Maintain clear distinction between the physical tool and a loan record. High-end educational editorial artifact, visually interesting yet simple.

Use case: productivity-visual. Asset: landscape 3:2 case-study illustration showing a complete Design Dash plan for a fictional neighborhood tool library. Match warm ivory paper, graphite, mustard accents and muted sage. Four elegant readable documents arranged in a deliberate 2x2 editorial board with thin unobtrusive alignment marks, restrained shallow paper shadows, not a boring flowchart. Headline "One decision, carried into the plan". Top left document heading "REQUIREMENT", exact short text "Show whether a tool can be borrowed." Smaller badge "Assumption to validate". Top right "OBJECT GUIDE", exact short text "Tool + Member + Loan", "One checked-out Loan per Tool." Bottom left "WIREFRAME": a clear simple flat app screen with a little outlined cordless drill, title "Cordless drill", status "Available", and one black button "Request to borrow"; a second small state pill "On loan · Due Friday". Bottom right "TECHNICAL NOTES", exact short text "Prevent overlapping checkouts.", "Recheck availability on confirmation.", "Test available and on-loan states." Along bottom a restrained set of 3 legible labels "Evidence & assumptions", "Research plan", "Stakeholder pitch". Small corner caption "ILLUSTRATIVE DASH ARTIFACTS". The image demonstrates aligned planning artifacts, not a shipped app or measured research. No accuracy percentages, no imagined quotes or users, no brands, no dense paragraphs. Typography large enough to read on a portfolio page.
Change only the phone screen status from Available to On loan so it matches the borrowing record and return action. Preserve the rest of the illustration.
